clue.text: Thrilling ride: at first boy and I gripped frantically

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word boy
frantically suggests wild disorder, so the letters of I gripped are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy and his friend cling on tight during a scary fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges I GRIPPED into IGDIPPER, placed after B.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a roller coaster, a classic fairground thrill ride, so the name fits a thrilling ride.

clue.text: Fun working in large hotel beginning to throw a tea party

indicators.note: in puts the reworked fun letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: big means large
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of throw
working means being worked over, so the letters of Fun are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big hotel puts on fun to start off a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns FUN into UNF, which goes 'in' BIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal term for a tea party, especially a noisy or chaotic one with buns.

clue.text: Understand start of gruesome film

indicators.note: start of picks out the first letter of gruesome

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's famous film

explanation.surface: Grasping the opening of a horror film.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: if you get a joke, you understand it.

clue.text: Silly section of refrain, an embarrassment

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a song's chorus is embarrassingly daft.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foolish, empty-headed or pointless remarks are silly.

clue.text: Having round agent, attractive

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the having word goes about the agent word

parts.note: possessing means having
a rep (representative) is a sales agent

explanation.surface: Having an agent around makes one appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: making a good first impression, appealing in looks or manner.

clue.text: Prize dog not right after run out

indicators.note: after places the trimmed dog word following the run-out letters

parts.note: RO is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: not tells us a letter is missing from the dog word

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A prize dog is disqualified after escaping from the show.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket scorecards RO marks a batsman run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon award given at shows, so it is a prize.

clue.text: Youngster in society lacking length

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped from the word for society

parts.note: a club is a society of members

explanation.surface: A young person who is out of place, or brief, in polite society.
explanation.definitionFit: A cub is a young animal, and also a junior Scout, so a youngster.

clue.text: Sister devoured by fish — odd riddle

indicators.note: devoured by means swallowed inside, so the sister goes into the fish

parts.note: a cod is a fish
a nun is a religious sister
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange puzzle about a nun eaten by a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a puzzling question or problem, often with a pun answer.

clue.text: Complaint from bishop over raised charge

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the bishop above the other piece

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the charge word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A grievance from a bishop about a fee increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a beef is a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Legal action taken by head, a very foolish person

indicators.note: taken by places the legal-action word after the head word, as if the head grabbed it

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a case is a lawsuit, a legal action

explanation.surface: A lawsuit brought by a company head who turns out to be a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone called crazy or idiotic is labelled this slang word.

clue.text: Seeing that Saint in church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: Noticing that a saint is commemorated in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions giving a reason: 'seeing that it rained' equals 'because it rained'.

clue.text: Incensed with anger, freebooter having lost power

indicators.note: having lost tells us a letter goes missing from the freebooter word

parts.note: a freebooter is a plunderer, a pirate
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A buccaneer stripped of his power is furious about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone incensed with anger is furious or enraged.

clue.text: Newscaster: can one run broadcast?

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of can one run are rearranged

explanation.surface: Can one person present a broadcast as newsreader?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a presenter who reads news on radio or television.

clue.text: Trip away and at home? Good

parts.note: someone away is out
at home is in

explanation.surface: A question about whether a trip counts as being away or at home, then praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a trip or excursion, such as a day out, is an outing.

clue.text: Accept members carry weapons

parts.note: to bear is to accept or tolerate
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Members of a group agree to be armed.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to go armed, as in the right to keep and carry firearms.

clue.text: Awfully good nurse here achieves academic success

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of good nurse here are reordered

explanation.surface: A very good nurse working here gains a university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-class or upper second degree with honours is a mark of university achievement.

clue.text: Improve ranking after winning

indicators.note: after puts the ranking word following the winning word

parts.note: up means ahead, as a team winning by a goal
a grade is a rank or level

explanation.surface: A player's ranking improves after victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to raise to a higher standard or better version.

clue.text: Critically appraises book

definitions.meaning: assesses or evaluates something as a critic would
the Book of ... in the Old Testament

explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning assesses, and also the Bible book named after Israel's early leaders.

clue.text: Almost reserved object

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the reserved word is cut

parts.note: demure means modest and reserved

explanation.surface: A shy, almost reserved, item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, so it means to object.

clue.text: Colour scheme in wide corridor

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words wide corridor

explanation.surface: A colour scheme in a broad hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is a room's furnishing and decoration style, including its colours.

clue.text: Cheese and English crackers served up

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Cheese and crackers presented together, English style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coating.

clue.text: Duke having a tea in a country house

parts.note: cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A duke takes tea in a stately home in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian second home in the countryside, a country house.

clue.text: In mouth of count is gold tooth

indicators.note: the mouth of a word is its opening, so only the first letter of count is taken

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A count has a gold tooth in his mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is one of the cutting front teeth, so it is a type of tooth.

clue.text: Spend time with someone in diocese

definitions.meaning: to date or meet with someone regularly
a bishop's seat or area of authority

explanation.definitionFit: A verb for dating or visiting a person, and the noun for a bishop's district.

clue.text: Damage sign, knocking end off

indicators.note: knocking end off removes the last letter of the word for sign

parts.note: a mark is a sign or indication

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises a signboard by knocking its end off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mar something is to spoil or impair it.

clue.text: Green seas generated enthusiasm

indicators.note: generated means produced anew, so the letters of Green seas are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Green seas stirred up excitement among sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: keenness or zeal, which is what enthusiasm describes.
